deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X is a (tame) stratified space with a closed stratum Y and open complement X* = X \ Y. V_{Y,X} is a tubular or germ neighbourhood of Y, and V*_{Y,X} = V_{Y,X} \ Y is the deleted neighbourhood. Under a normal local-triviality hypothesis, V*_{Y,X} → Y is a fibration. Its fibre is the local 'link' germ at a point of Y, written V*_{Z,Z} on the previous page (on this page Z, z and 2 are hard to distinguish). This is the topological counterpart of the punctured normal slice.

Previous page. The long exact homotopy sequence (12)/(13) of this fibration was written down.

This page draws the low-dimensional consequence.
- If the link is connected (Y does not locally disconnect X), then π1(V*_{Y,X}) is an extension of π1(Y) by the quotient of π1(link) by the image of the boundary map π2(Y) → π1(link).
- It is an extension by π1(link) itself if π2(Y) = 0 (or, more generally, if that boundary map is zero).
- In that case one gets diagram (14): a short exact sequence 1 → π1(link) → π1(V*_{Y,X}) → π1(Y) → 1, together with the map π1(V*_{Y,X}) → π1(X*) induced by the inclusion of the deleted neighbourhood into the open stratum.
- Grothendieck names π1(link) = I, the 'inertia' group, and π1(V*_{Y,X}) = D, the 'decomposition' group. This deliberately copies arithmetic: for a prime or a divisor, D_v → G_K, I_v ⊲ D_v, and D_v/I_v = π1 of the residue object = π1(Y).
- Diagram (14) refines his earlier diagram (10), which describes π1(X) (or the stratified fundamental groupoid) by gluing.

The K(π,1) case. Next he takes the 'pièces de construction' Y, X* and the link to be K(π,1)'s (15). The long exact sequence then shows that V*_{Y,X} is also a K(π,1). He adds that this holds trivially for the full neighbourhood V_{Y,X}, which is homotopy equivalent to Y.

Purpose. Everything is then encoded by a diagram of groups π1(Y) ← D → π1(X*) with I = ker(D → π1(Y)). The next page says that, given a flexible ('souple') theory of 'links of homotopy types', the whole homotopy type of X (not just its π1) should be expressible through this diagram of groups or groupoids. The next page also shows concretely that sheaves on X which are locally constant on each stratum are equivalent to triples (local system on X*, local system on Y, a morphism between their pullbacks to the deleted neighbourhood). That is a constructible-sheaf / exit-path description.

This is the general framework behind the Esquisse d'un programme picture: for moduli stacks M_{g,n}, the strata are K(π,1)'s, the inertia groups at boundary divisors are generated by Dehn twists, and the whole tower is reconstructed from 'Lego' pieces.
errors: Hypothesis (15) on X* is not needed to conclude that V*_{Y,X} is a K(π,1). It follows from the base Y and the link being K(π,1)'s, via the fibration's long exact sequence. X* matters only for the later gluing description of X.

Implicit hypotheses: Y connected, choice of base point, and V*_{Y,X} → Y a genuine (Serre) fibration. The last needs a normal local-triviality or Thom–Mather-type hypothesis, which Grothendieck mentions on the next page.
Unlike the arithmetic case (complete local fields), D → π1(X*) need not be injective topologically, so calling D a 'decomposition subgroup' is an analogy, not a literal subgroup statement.

Even if all the pieces are K(π,1)'s, X itself (the homotopy pushout of X* ← V*_{Y,X} → Y) need not be a K(π,1). Its homotopy type is that of a homotopy colimit of a diagram of BG's. Grothendieck seems aware of this, since he speaks of recovering the homotopy type, not just π1.

ideas.what: Fibration of the deleted tubular neighbourhood over the stratum with fibre the local link; the low-degree exact sequence gives 1 → π1(link) → π1(V*_{Y,X}) → π1(Y) → 1 when π2(Y) → π1(link) is zero.
ideas.modern_name: Link bundle / homotopy link fibration in stratified spaces (Quinn's homotopy links)

ideas.what: Calling π1(link) 'inertia' and π1(deleted neighbourhood) 'decomposition', with D/I = π1(stratum) and D → π1(open stratum): a topological dictionary for Galois decomposition and inertia groups.
ideas.modern_name: Topological inertia/decomposition groups at a divisor; tame fundamental group; inertia at boundary of moduli (Dehn twists)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Murre (tame fundamental group, 1971); SGA1 exp. XIII; Esquisse d'un programme (1984)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 XIII; Grothendieck–Murre LNM 208; Esquisse d'un programme §2–3 (inertia at the boundary of M_{g,n})

ideas.what: If the building pieces (strata and links) are K(π,1)'s, the deleted neighbourhoods are too, and the homotopy type of X is encoded by a diagram of groups or groupoids.
ideas.modern_name: Stratified homotopy type as a diagram of classifying spaces / complexes of groups; exit-path category with K(π,1) strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Haefliger / Bridson–Haefliger (complexes of groups); MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie (exit paths)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches a tame-topology programme along these lines

ideas.what: A hoped-for 'théorie souple des liens des types d'homotopie': a flexible homotopy theory of links that would reconstruct the homotopy type of a stratified space from pieces and gluing maps.
ideas.modern_name: Stratified homotopy hypothesis: exit-path ∞-categories / homotopy theory of stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, unpublished), Treumann 2009, Lurie HA App. A (2010s), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Haine, Douteau–Waas
ideas.where_published: Possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (tame topology, stratified structures)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a program: a 'flexible theory of links of homotopy types' in which the full homotopy type (not just π1) of a stratified space is expressed through the diagram (link → deleted neighbourhood → stratum, deleted neighbourhood → open stratum), with the inertia/decomposition terminology taken from arithmetic. This anticipates the exit-path / stratified homotopy hypothesis, realised much later by Treumann, Lurie, Haine and others, apparently without credit to these notes.
missed.quote: Si on a la "théorie souple des liens des types d'homotopie" à laquelle je faisais allusion, on devrait pouvoir exprimer alors le type d'homotopie de X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the stratified homotopy hypothesis. It also suggests an explicitly 'Galois-theoretic' (inertia/decomposition) formulation of exit-path categories, potentially useful for étale/profinite stratified homotopy types and anabelian questions about moduli spaces.

missed.claim: An explicit bridge between arithmetic decomposition/inertia groups and the topological link fibration of a stratified space, in the K(π,1) 'pièces de construction' regime. This is exactly the structure underlying the Teichmüller–Lego picture of the Esquisse, but here stated for general stratified spaces.
missed.quote: (I "inertie") ... (D "décomposition") ... Un cas intéressant est celui où les "pièces de construction" ... sont des espaces "K(π,1)"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a general stratified framework, as opposed to just normal-crossings divisors, for the inertia-at-the-boundary arguments used in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory and in anabelian geometry of moduli stacks.

deep.surprise_reason: The algebraic topology on the page is routine (the long exact sequence of a fibration). The interest lies in the explicit inertia/decomposition dictionary for strata in a general stratified setting, plus the announced program of a 'flexible theory of links of homotopy types', an early formulation of what became exit-path / stratified homotopy theory. Both themes are partly visible in the Esquisse, so this is not a striking new result.
transcription_corrections: 'V*_{2,2}' and 'V*_{Z,2}' are almost certainly the same object as V*_{Z,Z} on the previous page (the link germ at a point of Y); the '2' is a misreading of Z or z.
Line 2 'et = par π1(...) lui-même' should read 'et (une extension de π1(Y)) par π1(V*_{Z,Z}) lui-même si π2(Y) est nul'.
The struck-out word before 'que π2(Y) → ...' is a cancelled word (something like 'égal'), not mathematical content.
The struck-out text after '1 →' in (14) appears to be a cancelled 'Ker(...)', replaced by π1(V*_{Z,Z}).

The parenthetical at the end reads approximately '(et bien sûr pour V_{Y,X} ≃ Y homot.)', meaning the full neighbourhood is homotopy equivalent to Y. The image may show a star on V, but the homotopy equivalence with Y makes sense only for the undeleted neighbourhood.
